extra.reason: arch/ bundle established: index.md (okf_version 0.2), log.md, and ADR-0001..0003 as unreviewed drafts
Target suite named: sdk-unit in grizzly-platform/typescript (japa 5.0.0, 18 spec files, offline/DI). Recorded in ADR-0004. Consequence filed as cbd-cpy.
Gate A run on the target suite. It fails: phi = 51% on sdk-unit, so S_max = 0.49 at P=0. Result in FINDINGS.md section 10. Retarget-or-cancel filed separately.

Decided: retarget to the tests/stores suites. Gate A passes there at phi ~0.5% (548.6s floor-normalised). The unit-tests-only scope is reversed; the out-of-process instrumentation it removed is back in v1 as cbd-a3v, and it is now a prerequisite for Gate B.

inspectorSource contract defined: options shape, loopback/allowRemote security rule through the real entry point, target resolution, and a reusable Source contract suite (tests/support/source-contract.ts) now applied to both inProcessSource and an async-only stand-in. CDP client deliberately unbuilt; cbd-a3v owns it. 120 tests pass, up from 94.

Scope renamed @cbd/* to @spikedpunch/*: core -> @spikedpunch/cbd, mocha -> @spikedpunch/cbd-mocha, fixture and probe likewise; @cbd/auto became the subpath @spikedpunch/cbd/auto. 13 files plus the lockfile. Layout settled as hybrid rather than single-package: each framework adapter keeps its own peer dependency, so adapters stay sibling packages and ADR-0005 was amended to drop the single-package claim it had wrongly made. Verified by running every workspace: core 120, mocha 2, fixture 42, probe report clean. CBD.md 4.3 and 10 still describe the attach path as primary and still need aligning with ADR-0005.

The instrument module and its socket protocol are built and verified against the acceptance criteria: a compiled service importing nothing from CBD instruments under NODE_OPTIONS alone, a take names the functions it ran and not the ones it did not, the payload carries scriptParsed rows that resolve back to the TypeScript source, and close removes the socket without killing the service.

socketSource is built and satisfies the shared Source contract suite unchanged, supportsSync false with the dispatch-time window boundary, overlapping takes refused rather than queued, discovery refusing ambiguity rather than guessing, and per-process attribution verified across two independently driven services. The recording half of the acceptance clause (Recorder consuming an async source into a map) is a3v.3's subject and is noted as such on both issues.

QueuedSource built: dispatch()/drift() on socketSource, take() refuses while a dispatch is outstanding, and the partition property is asserted rather than reasoned. 23 tests in socket-source.spec.ts, stable over 3 runs; core 148 green, workspace 224. Measured the drift the task asked about: it is a function of queue depth, not a constant (68us at 0.5ms spacing, 24ms at 200 back-to-back), so maxDepth is reported as the predicting variable and a characterisation test pins where the design stops working.

Recorder defers: one bookkeeping path, a Windows strategy for the only thing that differs, drained() to await. Evidence: byte-identical shard text from both recorders on the same payloads, and the 7 pre-existing recorder tests pass unchanged. A0 F12 probed: japa DOES await an async runner:end listener, so the drain can live there. Two bugs found by the comparison test (fire-and-forget queue helper; duration computed inside the deferred builder) and one checking bug (build piped to tail masked a failing typecheck). core 153, japa 28, workspace 231, stable over 3 runs.

Adapter drives a list of recorders off one set of boundaries, finish() awaits every drain; plugin opens [test process, service] when CBD_SOCKET_DIR is set, deriving the service shard path and carrying the service pid. Unreachable service is an error, not a silent fallback. Verified (not assumed) that two shards naming one test UNION its touches in buildMap, and that pid is provenance not identity. japa 36, core 155, workspace 239 green with exit 0, stable x3; smackdebt clean on packages/japa/src.

A service started the way a developer starts one (NODE_OPTIONS, nothing imported from CBD), a japa suite driving it over HTTP, a map built from both shards. Attribution measured rather than argued: storeKey to exactly one test, fetchKey to exactly the other (which is what separates a window from a running total), rotateMasterKey to nothing while its file is known, and an inert test recorded with a window holding none of the service. Running it found two defects the unit-level wiring could not: the recorded run never exited because the socket source was never closed (fixed: Recorder#close, called after the drains), and scripts with no source map and no projection rule were dropped from the map entirely because an empty rule list was read as no-rule-matched (fixed in source-maps.ts, tested). A third finding, CBD's own code landing in every window it serves, is filed as cbd-qly rather than absorbed.

Drift measured per window in a real run (mean 0.27-0.85ms against boundaries 9.4-14.6ms apart) and the @between residual measured at zero for the service's own execution. Decision: neither tighten nor loosen, recorded against those numbers in arch/log.md. Correction of record: maxDepth does not mean boundary slide, and said it did; docblocks fixed, cbd-llm filed for the first-take stall it actually measures.

Fixed in rescanningSocketSource: new sockets are attached by a 25ms background scan (unref'd, cleared on close) so the boundary's take has no async connect to wait on; an attach still in flight at a boundary is chained into that window's take instead of being skipped, so a socket that appeared late in a window is not credited to the next one. core 172 passed; japa 61 passed; own-service-e2e 6/6, repeated 3x.

Method E landed (ack op, per-take retention, pid-<pid>.coverage.json written after each take and every 500ms and at exit, recovery by take id or untaken accumulator, stderr loudness for unrecoverable windows) plus cbd-ot8's early attach. core 172 passed; japa 61 passed; own-service-e2e 6/6.
